Question:
Given that the patient is 61.7 years old, will the cancer have a recurrence in the next 24 months?
A) Yes
B) No
explanation:
The patient, diagnosed with Stage III pancreatic head adenocarcinoma (AJCC III), underwent an aggressive multimodal neoadjuvant treatment course consisting of two cycles of FOLFIRINOX (leucovorin, oxaliplatin, fluorouracil, irinotecan) and radiation therapy, followed by surgical resection at age 61.589. Throughout treatment, his CA 19-9 levels demonstrated a sustained, dramatic biochemical response, dropping from a peak of 1,443 Units/ml down to 56 Units/ml post-surgery (age 61.687). Furthermore, sequential CT scans consistently confirmed no disease progression, with post-operative imaging at ages 61.602 and 61.668 showing no detectable cancer (HAS_CANCER: No).

Despite this strong initial response and successful resection, Stage III pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma carries an extremely high baseline risk of recurrence—historically exceeding 70–80% within the first two years even after neoadjuvant chemoradiation and surgery—particularly given his persistently elevated post-operative CA 19-9 (56 Units/ml, above the normal reference threshold of <37 Units/ml), which indicates likely minimal residual disease.

Throughout treatment, his CA 19-9 levels demonstrated a sustained, dramatic biochemical response, dropping from a peak of 1,443 Units/ml down to 56 Units/ml post-surgery (age 61.687). Furthermore, sequential CT scans consistently confirmed no disease progression, with post-operative imaging at ages 61.602 and 61.668 showing no detectable cancer (HAS_CANCER: No).

[ANSWER: A) Yes]

explanation:
The patient (P-0006687) was initially diagnosed at age 53.37 with Stage IV (AJCC IV, Clinical Group 4A) microsatellite-stable (MSS) sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma harboring a TP53 missense mutation (p.C242F), CTNNB1 exon 3 splice-site deletion (p.X6_splice), CDK12 nonsense mutation (p.S238*), and ERBB2 copy number amplification (value 2.0).

Following initial FOLFOX therapy (oxaliplatin, leucovorin, fluorouracil), the patient experienced intra-abdominal disease progression at age 54.99 (accompanied by a CEA spike to 4.2 ng/ml). Subsequent treatment with FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab, followed by surgical resection and hepatic arterial infusion floxuridine at age 55.63, successfully cleared radiographic disease (HAS CANCER: No at ages 55.44, 55.78, and 55.86) and normalized CEA levels (0.8–1.1 ng/ml through age 55.86). However, given the underlying Stage IV metastatic biology, ERBB2 amplification, and TP53 mutation—alongside the prior rapid relapse following first-line systemic therapy—the risk of another recurrence within the subsequent 12 months remains high.

Disease Trajectory & Metastatic Burden: Following initial resection and adjuvant therapy, the patient developed liver metastases at age 64.73. After a prolonged disease control period on FOLFIRINOX (ages 64.78–66.31), the patient experienced rapid multisite radiographic progression at age 66.36 (new lymph node metastases alongside liver involvement) and further progression at age 66.59 with the development of bone metastases, which carry a particularly poor prognosis in metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

Biomarker Kinetics: Tumor markers surged exponentially alongside radiographic progression—CA 19-9 rose from 60 U/mL (age 65.41) to 1,045 U/mL (age 66.09) and peaked at 7,861 U/mL (age 66.54), while CEA climbed from 3.2 ng/mL to 44.5 ng/mL (age 66.54).

Treatment Outlook: Despite initiating second-line systemic therapy with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel at age 66.37–66.39, repeat imaging two months later (age 66.59) demonstrated continued disease progression into bone with persistently elevated tumor markers (CA 19-9: 5,870 U/mL; CEA: 38.8 ng/mL). Refractory metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma progressing through both FOLFIRINOX and gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel with hepatic, nodal, and osseous involvement has a median overall survival well under 6 months, making 12-month survival highly unlikely.

In heavily pretreated recurrent pancreatic adenocarcinoma, a nearly tenfold rebound in CA 19-9 strongly precedes overt radiographic progression within a 12-month window.

This was managed with curative-intent liver surgery (age 57.17) and adjuvant hepatic arterial infusion (HAI) floxuridine plus systemic FOLFIRI (leucovorin, fluorouracil, irinotecan) completed at age 57.67.

Sustained Remission & Surveillance (timeline2.txt): Throughout the entire surveillance period from age 57.8 to 58.9 (over 14 months post-chemotherapy), the patient has maintained complete disease-free status:

Performance Status: The patient maintains an optimal functional baseline (ECOG 0–1).

Despite a prior oligometastatic liver recurrence over two years ago, definitive surgical resection combined with adjuvant HAI floxuridine and systemic FOLFIRI achieved a durable complete remission. With over a year of negative cross-sectional surveillance imaging and flat, low-normal CEA levels leading up to age 59, the probability of recurrence within the next 12 months is low.

A) Yes
B) No
explanation:
Based on the provided clinical, pathological, and genomic records for patient P-0022916:

Disease Course & Oligometastatic Control: The patient was initially diagnosed at age 54.85 with localized Stage 2A microsatellite-stable (MSS) rectal adenocarcinoma (TP53 and APC mutated, KRAS/BRAF wild-type), treated with neoadjuvant/adjuvant FOLFOX and primary resection (age 55.29). At age 57.11, the patient developed an isolated hepatic recurrence accompanied by a CEA spike to 10.1 ng/mL. However, this oligometastatic liver disease was aggressively and successfully treated via hepatic surgery (age 57.17) followed by hepatic arterial infusion (HAI) floxuridine and systemic FOLFIRI (irinotecan, fluorouracil, leucovorin) through age 57.67.

Sustained Complete Remission: Following the completion of treatment for the liver metastasis, serial CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis from age 57.18 through age 58.90 consistently show no evidence of cancer (HAS CANCER: No) and no disease progression.

Biomarker & Clinical Stability: Serum CEA levels normalized immediately post-resection and have remained completely stable within the normal reference range (1.5–1.6 ng/mL) throughout the entire preceding year (ages 58.34 to 58.86). Additionally, the patient maintains an excellent functional status (ECOG 0–1) and is off active chemotherapy without signs of toxicity or clinical decline.

Given the sustained radiographic complete remission, normalized and stable CEA levels for nearly two years post-metastasectomy, and strong performance status, the patient has a very favorable prognosis to remain alive over the next 12 months.

A) Yes

explanation:
Based on the available clinical, pathological, and genomic records for patient P-0022916, the cancer is unlikely to progress over the next 12 months.

Clinical & Pathological Summary

Diagnosis & Genomics: Initially diagnosed at age 54.85 with Stage IIA localized, microsatellite-stable (MSS) rectal adenocarcinoma (TMB: 6.92 mut/Mb) harboring canonical APC and TP53 (p.R175H) mutations.

Recurrence & Definitive Salvage Therapy: Following initial neoadjuvant/adjuvant FOLFOX and primary resection, the patient experienced an isolated hepatic recurrence at age 57.11 accompanied by a CEA spike to 10.1 ng/mL. This was aggressively managed via surgical resection (age 57.17) followed by hepatic arterial infusion (HAI) floxuridine combined with systemic FOLFIRI through age 57.67.

Sustained Remission (Ages 57.18 – 58.90): Post-resection and post-chemotherapy surveillance demonstrates nearly two full years of complete disease control:

Serial Imaging: Five consecutive chest/abdomen/pelvis CT scans between ages 57.93 and 58.90 consistently report no evidence of cancer (HAS CANCER: No) and no progression.

Tumor Markers: Serial CEA levels have remained completely normalized and stable (1.5–1.6 ng/mL from age 58.34 through 58.86), showing no biochemical trend toward relapse.

Performance Status: The patient maintains an excellent functional baseline (ECOG 0–1) off active chemotherapy for over 1.2 years.

Given the sustained radiological complete response, flat normal CEA trajectory, and prolonged treatment-free interval following curative-intent hepatic resection and HAI/systemic therapy, the risk of progression in the subsequent 12 months is low.

explanation:
Based on the clinical, molecular, and imaging records provided for patient P-0027883, the prognosis for 12-month survival from age 50.2 is favorable, and the patient is likely to remain alive.

Clinical and Molecular Summary

Primary Diagnosis & Molecular Profile: The patient was diagnosed at age 48.5 with Stage IIB (pT3N1) infiltrating ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head (KRAS p.G12V, TP53 p.C275Y, and homozygous deletions in CDKN2A/B and SMAD4; MSS, TMB 2.6 mut/Mb). Following surgical resection (age 48.55), they completed adjuvant gemcitabine and capecitabine (ages 48.65–49.09).

Recurrence & Therapeutic Response: Disease progression/recurrence was identified on CT and PET imaging around age 49.76. Systemic salvage therapy with FOLFIRINOX (fluorouracil, leucovorin, irinotecan, oxaliplatin) was initiated at age 49.80 and administered through age 50.05.

Current Disease Control & Functional Status:

Radiographic Stability: Follow-up CT scans (ages 49.94 and 50.06) and PET imaging (age 50.06) confirm that the disease has not progressed following FOLFIRINOX, transitioning into consolidative chemoradiation (capecitabine starting age 50.07 and radiation therapy at age 50.11).

Biomarkers: Tumor markers remain consistently within normal limits, with CA 19-9 stable at 22–24 Units/mL (normal <37 Units/mL) and CEA at 1.1–1.2 ng/mL.

Performance Status: The patient maintains an excellent functional status (ECOG 0–1) through age 50.15, supporting continued tolerance of active therapy.

Given the documented disease stabilization on systemic chemotherapy, transition to consolidative chemoradiation, normal tumor markers, and preserved performance status (ECOG 0–1), the patient is expected to survive the next 12 months.

explanation:
Based on the clinical, molecular, and imaging data provided, yes, the patient's cancer is likely to progress within the next 12 months.

Aggressive Disease Biology & Confirmed Recurrence: The patient has Stage IIB infiltrating pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (MSS, TMB 2.59 mut/Mb) harboring classic high-risk alterations (KRAS p.G12V, TP53 p.C275Y, and homozygous deletions of SMAD4 and CDKN2A/B). Following initial surgical resection at age 48.55 and adjuvant gemcitabine/capecitabine, the patient experienced confirmed disease progression on CT at age 49.755 with new PET-avid disease in the head/neck region (age 49.766) and rising CA 19-9 (from 15–17 U/mL up to 24 U/mL).

Limited Durability of Salvage Therapy: Although salvage FOLFIRINOX (ages 49.799–50.048) followed by capecitabine-based chemoradiation (starting at age 50.070) achieved temporary radiographic disease stabilization at age 50.059, active tumor presence persists on both CT (chest/abdomen/pelvis) and PET (head), and CA 19-9 remains plateaued at 22–24 U/mL without returning to baseline.

Prognostic Outlook: In recurrent pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma—particularly with KRAS G12V, TP53, and SMAD4 loss—median progression-free survival following second-line systemic therapy and chemoradiation is typically under 6 to 12 months, making further disease progression within the next year highly probable.

Question:
Given that the patient is 51.3 years old, will the cancer have a recurrence in the next 12 months?
A) Yes
B) No
explanation:
Clinical & Pathological Assessment

Initial Presentation & Genomics (Age ~48.5): Diagnosed with Stage IIB (pathological group 2B) infiltrating ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head (KRAS p.G12V, TP53 p.C275Y, homozygous deletions in SMAD4, CDKN2A, and CDKN2B, microsatellite stable [MSS], TMB 2.59 mut/Mb). Underwent primary surgical resection followed by adjuvant gemcitabine and capecitabine.

First Recurrence & Salvage Therapy (Age 49.7–50.2): At age 49.755, surveillance CT/PET identified disease progression/recurrence, accompanied by a mild CA 19-9 rise to 24 U/mL. The patient received salvage FOLFIRINOX (leucovorin, irinotecan, oxaliplatin, fluorouracil) followed by capecitabine-based chemoradiation (completed at age 50.166).

Post-Salvage Surveillance & Complete Remission (Age 50.2–51.3):

Following chemoradiation, serial CT and PET scans from age 50.500 through 51.229 consistently demonstrated no evidence of active cancer (HAS CANCER: No) and no disease progression across the chest, abdomen, pelvis, and head—indicating a complete clinical and metabolic response.

Serum CA 19-9 declined from 28 U/mL (age 50.251) and remained stably normalized between 14 and 16 U/mL (well below the 37 U/mL upper limit of normal) for over 8 months up to age 51.229.

The patient maintained an excellent performance status (ECOG 0) off systemic therapy for nearly a full year.

Given the sustained complete radiological and metabolic remission on serial PET/CT scans, stably low normal CA 19-9 levels (14–16 U/mL), and an extended progression-free interval of over 12 months following salvage FOLFIRINOX and chemoradiation, a recurrence within the next 12 months is unlikely.

CEA remained stable within normal limits (1.3–2.5 ng/mL), and the patient maintained an ECOG performance status of 0 at age 74.633.

Given her complete radiographic and biochemical remission immediately preceding age 71.6, short-term progression within the next 12 months is not expected.   
UT MD Anderson Cancer Center

Clinical and Molecular Evaluation

Clinical & Treatment History: The patient was diagnosed at age 70.50 with localized/regional (Stage 2A/2B) pancreatic tail adenocarcinoma and underwent surgical resection (AGE: 70.546), followed by two courses of adjuvant FOLFIRINOX (fluorouracil, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, leucovorin) between ages 70.629 and 71.089, maintaining an ECOG performance status of 0.

Genomic Risk Profile: The primary tumor harbors three major pancreatic adenocarcinoma driver alterations: KRAS p.G12R, TP53 p.R273C, and homozygous deletion of SMAD4 (-2.0). Combined with the abrupt biochemical rebound in CA 19-9 above the normal threshold following completion of FOLFIRINOX, early recurrence within the next 6 months is likely.

Clinical & Genomic Assessment

Genomic Profile (High-Risk Molecular Drivers):

The tumor harbors a classic triad of aggressive pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) driver alterations: activating KRAS p.G12R mutation, TP53 p.R273C missense mutation, and SMAD4 homozygous deletion (VALUE = -2.0).

Co-occurring alterations in KRAS, TP53, and SMAD4 (specifically SMAD4 loss/inactivation) are strongly associated with aggressive tumor biology, early systemic dissemination, impaired response to FOLFIRINOX chemotherapy, and a high rate of early postoperative recurrence.

Diagnosis & Surgery: Diagnosed at age 70.5 with primary pancreatic tail adenocarcinoma (Stage IIB, regional nodal involvement) and underwent surgical resection at age 70.546.

In resected PDAC, a rapid post-treatment CA 19-9 surge preceding or accompanying radiological follow-up is a classic harbinger of impending clinical and radiographic progression.

Given the aggressive triple-driver molecular profile (KRAS, TP53, and SMAD4 loss), Stage IIB regional disease, and the sharp post-chemotherapy rebound in CA 19-9 at age 71.166, disease progression within the next 12 months is highly likely.

explanation:
Based on the clinical timeline and genomic profile, the patient is at very high risk for a cancer recurrence within the next 6 months:

Aggressive Disease Trajectory & Prior Relapse: Initially diagnosed at age 71.068 with stage IIA (PATH_GROUP: 2A) microsatellite-stable (MSS) ascending colon/cecum adenocarcinoma, the patient experienced a rapid metastatic relapse to the liver within less than a year (at age 72.035, accompanied by a CEA spike to 14.0 ng/mL).

High-Risk Molecular Profile: Next-generation sequencing (IMPACT468) reveals co-occurring driver mutations in KRAS (p.G12V), TP53 (p.R273C and p.A159P), PIK3CA (p.E542K), and APC. Combined KRAS and TP53 mutations in right-sided, MSS colorectal cancer are strongly associated with chemoresistance, higher recurrence rates following liver metastasis resection, and poor disease-free survival.   
Baishideng Publishing Group

Biochemical Relapse & Treatment Cessation: Following liver surgery (age 72.123) and adjuvant FOLFOX chemotherapy (ages 72.202–72.5475), the patient's CEA initially dropped to 4.3 ng/mL (age 72.202) but more than doubled to 8.7 ng/mL at age 72.600—immediately after stopping chemotherapy. Although cross-sectional imaging (CT, PET, MR) at ages 72.600–72.668 has not yet detected a macroscopic lesion (HAS CANCER: No), a rising CEA above normal limits following metastasectomy and systemic therapy is a classic early indicator of occult/microscopic recurrence that precedes radiographic detection by several months.

Tumor markers remain stably within normal limits through age 51.55 (CA 19-9: 11–14 U/mL; CEA: 1.3–2.5 ng/mL).

Given complete surgical resection, full completion of adjuvant FOLFIRINOX (with potential platinum sensitization via FANCC mutation), sustained normal tumor markers, and negative surveillance imaging right up to age 51.55, a recurrence within the immediate next 6 months is unlikely.

Treatment & Recurrence: Following surgical resection (age 50.96) and adjuvant FOLFIRINOX (ages 51.08–51.51), the patient initially achieved radiographic remission. Prognosis: Metastatic, chemo-refractory KRAS/TP53-mutant pancreatic adenocarcinoma with widespread multi-organ involvement and a rapidly escalating CA 19-9 > 2,000 U/mL carries an extremely poor prognosis, with median overall survival typically measured in only a few months.

Question:
Given that the patient is 61.6 years old, will the cancer have a recurrence in the next 12 months?
A) Yes
B) No
explanation:
Clinical & Genomic Assessment

Disease Staging & Treatment Course:

The patient was diagnosed at age 60.52 with Stage IIB (Pathological Group 2B, regional spread) pancreatic body adenocarcinoma (C25.1), which carries a high baseline risk of early relapse.

Following surgical resection (age 60.59) and adjuvant FOLFIRINOX chemotherapy (oxaliplatin, leucovorin, irinotecan, fluorouracil from age 60.74 to 61.18), surveillance imaging through age 61.52 shows no radiographic evidence of cancer progression.

Tumor Markers & Surveillance Dynamics:

While CA 19-9 initially declined during chemotherapy (from 70 U/mL to 39–49 U/mL), it experienced a transient spike to 121 U/mL at age 61.29 (shortly after completing chemotherapy, coinciding with an indeterminate pelvic/abdominal MR finding at age 61.28), before settling back to 52 U/mL at age 61.52 (still persistently above the normal <37 U/mL reference range).

CEA has shown a gradual upward drift from 2.3 ng/mL at baseline to 3.1–3.6 ng/mL in recent follow-ups.

Molecular & Genomic Profile:

MSK-IMPACT sequencing reveals a microsatellite-stable (MSS), low-TMB (2.59 mut/Mb) tumor harboring concurrent KRAS (p.G12V) and truncating TP53 (p.S95Lfs*28) frameshift mutations, alongside a nonsense TP53BP1 (p.E662*) mutation.

Co-occurring KRAS and truncating TP53 alterations in resected Stage IIB pancreatic adenocarcinoma are strongly associated with aggressive tumor biology, early recurrence (peak incidence within the first 12–24 months post-resection), and shorter recurrence-free survival.   
Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center

Given the Stage IIB nodal/regional involvement, high-risk KRAS G12V + truncating TP53 co-mutation profile, and persistently elevated post-treatment CA 19-9, the patient is at high risk for disease recurrence within the next 12 months.

Question:
Given that the patient is 69 years old, will the cancer have a recurrence in the next 6 months?
A) Yes
B) No
explanation:
Clinical Evaluation & Evidence Summary

Diagnosis & Pathology: Localized Stage IIA (PATH_GROUP: 2A, SUMMARY: Localized) mucinous adenocarcinoma of the colon (P-0043580-T01-IM6), microsatellite stable (MSI_TYPE: Stable, MMR_ABSENT: False), with somatic alterations in APC, KRAS (p.G13D, p.V14I), GNAS (p.R201H), SOX9, AMER1, and KDM6A.

Clinical Course & Surveillance: Following surgical resection around age 66.8–66.9, serial CT imaging of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis at ages 67.483 and 68.497 confirmed no evidence of cancer (HAS CANCER: No) and no progression. Performance status improved and remained optimal (ECOG: 0 at age 68.502).

Biomarker Trajectory: Post-resection CEA levels dropped from 10.0 ng/mL to a stable normal baseline (0.9–1.5 ng/mL) for nearly two years. At the end of the observation window (age 68.979), CEA rose slightly to 4.0 ng/mL—a mild, isolated elevation still within or near the upper limit of normal without radiological evidence of disease.

Given the localized stage at resection, sustained two-year disease-free survival on surveillance CT scans, ECOG 0 status, and absence of confirmed radiographic recurrence, short-term recurrence within the next 6 months at age 69 is unlikely.

Genomic profiling shows microsatellite stability (MSS), low tumor mutational burden (0.86 mut/Mb), and a somatic NKX2-1 frameshift insertion without aggressive driver alterations (such as KRAS, TP53, or STK11).

Recent Disease Course (Ages 50.0–50.8): While interim scans at ages 50.12 and 50.26 flagged suspected residual/recurrent findings prompting tissue sampling/procedures (ages 50.16 and 50.27), subsequent serial imaging—including brain/spine MRIs (ages 50.18, 50.37) and chest CTs (ages 50.39, 50.67)—consistently demonstrated no cancer progression and ultimately showed no evidence of cancer (HAS CANCER: No) at age 50.67.

Performance Status: Functional status improved from ECOG 1 at age 50.13 back to ECOG 0 (fully active, asymptomatic) by age 50.68.

Given the sustained absence of disease progression over more than three years since diagnosis, negative restaging CT at age 50.67, and an ECOG 0 performance status, the patient has a favorable short-term prognosis and is expected to remain alive over the next 12 months.

Clinical & Surveillance Analysis

Diagnosis & Staging: The patient was diagnosed at age 49.73 with primary upper-lobe lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), pathological stage IIB (PATH_GROUP: 2B, regional lymph node involvement), with an initial ECOG performance status of 0.

Treatment History: Following surgical resection at age 49.79, the patient completed adjuvant chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel between ages 50.00 and 50.18.

Radiographic Surveillance: Serial chest CT scans performed regularly post-surgery and post-chemotherapy—at ages 49.88, 50.32, 50.83, 51.32, and 51.84—consistently show no evidence of active disease (HAS CANCER: No) and no progression (CT scan reveals cancer has NOT progressed).

Genomic Profile: The tumor exhibits a typical LUSC molecular profile (3q26 amplification involving SOX2, TP63, DCUN1D1; 11q13 amplification involving CCND1, FGF3/4/19; and somatic mutations in TP53, CDKN2A, PIK3CA, and NOTCH1), without progressive clinical behavior over more than two years of follow-up.

Given over two years of sustained radiographic remission following definitive surgical resection and adjuvant platinum-taxane chemotherapy, recurrence within the next 12 months is unlikely.

Question:
Given that the patient is 64.1 years old, will the patient be still alive in the next 24 months?
A) Yes
B) No
explanation:
The patient is a 64.1-year-old with metastatic rectal adenocarcinoma (originally diagnosed as Stage I localized disease at age 58.1) who developed pulmonary and hepatic metastases around ages 60.8–61.1.

Key clinical, pathological, and molecular factors indicate a favorable 24-month prognosis from age 64.1:

Disease Control and Response to Therapy: Following systemic FOLFOX chemotherapy (fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin administered from ages 62.89 to 63.33), Yttrium-90 radioembolization (age 62.71), and surgical intervention (age 63.61), serial restaging scans (PET at 63.08 and 63.35, MRI at 63.96, and CT at 64.07) demonstrate complete resolution of detectable disease (HAS CANCER: No) with no evidence of recent progression.

Biomarker Stability: Serum CEA levels have remained consistently normal throughout the entire disease course (1.0–1.4 ng/ml, most recently 1.3 ng/ml at age 64.07).

Molecular Profile: While the tumor harbors TP53 (p.R158H) and APC (p.R213*) mutations and is microsatellite stable (MSS), its BRAF mutation is an atypical Class 3 kinase-impaired variant (BRAF D594G), rather than the aggressive V600E mutation. In metastatic colorectal cancer, non-V600E BRAF D594G mutations are associated with significantly longer overall survival compared to BRAF V600E and even BRAF wild-type cohorts, particularly in patients achieving disease control after metastasectomy or multimodal local/systemic therapy.

Performance Status: The patient maintains a good functional baseline (ECOG 1).

Given the absence of active radiologic disease, normal CEA levels, favorable atypical BRAF D594G biology, and good performance status, the patient is expected to survive beyond the next 24 months.
